facts.statement: The genus Patagotitan was described by Carballido and colleagues in 2017.
facts.quote: authority: Carballido et al., 2017

facts.statement: Patagotitan lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Albian stage.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous (Albian),

facts.statement: Fossils of Patagotitan were found in the Cerro Barcino Formation in Chubut Province, Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: Patagotitan is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous (Albian stage) Cerro Barcino Formation in Chubut Province, Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: Early estimates suggested Patagotitan was the largest known land animal, measuring 37 meters long and weighing 69 tonnes.
facts.quote: Originally thought to be the largest known titanosaur and land animal overall, preliminary studies and press releases suggested that Patagotitan had an estimated length of 37 m and an estimated weight of 69 tonne.

facts.statement: Later research revised Patagotitan's size to approximately 31 meters in length and 50 to 60 tonnes in weight.
facts.quote: Later research revised the length estimate down to 31 m and weight estimates down to approximately 50 - 60 tonne, suggesting that Patagotitan was of a similar size to, if not smaller than, its closest relatives Argentinosaurus and Puertasaurus.

facts.statement: Patagotitan is distinguished from relatives by unique features in its vertebrae, shoulder bones, forelimb bones, and hindlimb bones.
facts.quote: It can be distinguished from its close relatives by a suite of unique characteristics in its back and tail vertebrae, scapulae and humeri in the forelimb, and ischia and femora in the hindlimb.

facts.statement: Patagotitan possessed a unique weight-bearing adaptation where hyposphene-hypantrum articulations were found between only one pair of vertebrae, unlike other sauropods.
facts.quote: Among these was the presence of accessory vertebral articulations known as the hyposphene-hypantrum articulations between only one pair of vertebrae at the level of the scapular blade, which was likely a weight-bearing adaptation not seen in any other sauropod (where they were either present between all pairs or between none).

facts.statement: Patagotitan lived in a forested floodplain environment dominated by coniferous trees.
facts.quote: In life, Patagotitan lived in a forested region on a floodplain that was dominated by coniferous trees.

facts.statement: A partial lower femur was discovered in 2010 by a farm laborer near La Flecha, Argentina.
facts.quote: A part of a lower femur was discovered in 2010 by a farm laborer, Aurelio Hernández, in the desert near La Flecha, Argentina, about 250 km west of Trelew.

facts.statement: The rock layers containing Patagotitan fossils are dated to approximately 101.62 million years ago.
facts.quote: The rock layers at the La Flecha site belong to the Cerro Castaño Member of the Cerro Barcino Formation, and were specifically dated to approximately 101.62 million years in age (corresponding to the latest Albian age of the Cretaceous).

facts.statement: The collected fossils represent at least six partial skeletons that likely belonged to the same species, differing by no more than 5% in length.
facts.quote: The collected sauropod fossils were organized into six partial skeletons, which likely belonged to the same species due to uniformity in their morphology and size (with all individuals differing no more than 5% in length).

facts.statement: The fossils were found in a 3.43-meter sediment layer containing three distinct levels corresponding to three separate burial events.
facts.quote: Within the 3.43 m sediment layer containing the fossils, there are three distinct but closely-spaced levels corresponding to three burial events, which are named FLV1, FLV2, and FLV3.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, catalogued as MPEF-PV 3400, was a partial skeleton from the FLV3 burial level.
facts.quote: One skeleton from FLV3 was designated as the holotype specimen of a new species, and was catalogued as MPEF-PV 3400.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton lacks a skull but includes neck vertebrae, back vertebrae, tail vertebrae, ribs, sternum plates, shoulder girdle elements, pubic bones, and femora.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull, with three neck vertebrae, six back vertebrae, six front tail vertebrae, three chevrons, ribs, both plates of the sternum and the right scapulocoracoid in the shoulder girdle, both pubic bones, and both femora.

facts.statement: In 2017, a team led by José Luis Carballido named the remains Patagotitan mayorum.
facts.quote: In 2017, José Luis Carballido, Diego Pol, Alejandro Otero, Ignacio Alejandro Cerda, Leonardo Salgado, Alberto Carlos Garrido, Jahandar Ramezani, Néstor Ruben Cúneo and Javier Marcelo Krause named these remains as the type species of a new genus, Patagotitan mayorum.

facts.statement: The name Patagotitan combines a reference to Patagonia with the Greek word for Titan to reflect its strength and large size.
facts.quote: The generic name combines a reference to Patagonia with a Greek Titan for the "strength and large size" of this titanosaur.

facts.statement: The specific name mayorum honors the Mayo family, who owned the La Flecha ranch.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the Mayo family, owners of La Flecha ranch.

facts.statement: The known remains make Patagotitan one of the most completely known members of the Titanosauria.
facts.quote: Collectively, the known remains made Patagotitan one of the most completely-known members of the Titanosauria.

facts.statement: A quarry excavated 300 meters west revealed a fourth sediment layer containing a similarly sized sauropod skeleton.
facts.quote: Another quarry was excavated about 300 m west, revealing a fourth sediment layer (FLV4) with a similarly sized sauropod skeleton.

facts.statement: Patagotitan was used in the re-definition of the group Colossosauria in 2022.
facts.quote: This led to its use in a re-definition of the group Colossosauria by Carballido and colleagues in 2022.

facts.statement: Patagotitan belongs to the clade Lognkosauria and is a particularly large and robust titanosaur.
facts.quote: Like Argentinosaurus and other members of its clade, Lognkosauria, Patagotitan was a particularly large and robust titanosaur.

facts.statement: Skeletal mounts of Patagotitan are displayed in multiple museums.
facts.quote: Skeletal mounts based on all available material of Patagotitan are displayed in multiple museums.

facts.statement: A skeletal mount of Patagotitan is exhibited in the Museum of Paleontology Egidio Feruglio.
facts.quote: One mount is exhibited in the Museum of Paleontology Egidio Feruglio.

facts.statement: A mount of Patagotitan is exhibited at the American Museum of Natural History, replacing a juvenile Barosaurus mount.
facts.quote: Another is exhibited in the American Museum of Natural History, where it replaced a juvenile Barosaurus mount.

facts.statement: A mount of Patagotitan is exhibited at the Field Museum of Natural History, where it replaced the Sue specimen of Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: One is exhibited in the Field Museum of Natural History, where it replaced the Sue specimen of Tyrannosaurus (which has been moved to another exhibit).

facts.statement: A mount of Patagotitan was displayed at the Natural History Museum, London, from March 2023 to January 2024.
facts.quote: From March 2023 until January 2024, one was displayed at the Natural History Museum, London.

facts.statement: Patagotitan was a large, quadrupedal herbivore characterized by a long neck and tail.
facts.quote: Like other titanosaur sauropods, Patagotitan was a quadrupedal herbivore with a long neck and tail and is notable for its large size.

facts.statement: Early media reports in 2014 estimated Patagotitan to be 40 meters long and weigh 77 tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2014 news reports provided estimates of Patagotitan size at 40 m long with a weight of 77 tonne.

facts.statement: A 2017 study estimated Patagotitan's length at 37 meters and its weight between 44.2 and 77.6 tonnes using volumetric methods.
facts.quote: In 2017, Carballido and colleagues published a length estimate of 37 m, and provided two weight estimates: 69 tonne using a scaling equation, and 44.2 - 77.6 t using volumetric method based on 3D skeletal models.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Gregory S. Paul estimated Patagotitan to be 31 meters long and weigh between 50 and 55 tonnes in 2019.
facts.quote: In 2019 Gregory S. Paul estimated Patagotitan at 31 m in length and 50 - 55 t in weight using volumetric models.

facts.statement: A 2020 study by Campione and Evans calculated Patagotitan's body mass at approximately 55.7 tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2020, Campione and Evans yielded a body mass estimate of approximately 55.7 t.

facts.statement: Otero and Carballido estimated Patagotitan's mean weight at 57 tonnes with a margin of error ranging from 42.5 to 71.4 tonnes in 2020.
facts.quote: In 2020, Otero and Carballido published a lower mean weight estimate of 57 t using a revised scaling equation, with a margin of error of 42.5 – 71.4 t

facts.statement: Bone histology reveals that the Patagotitan specimens died as young adults when their growth had slowed but not stopped.
facts.quote: Histology of five femora and one humerus indicates that the individuals died while they were young adults, with growth having slowed but not ceased entirely.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul argued in 2019 that Patagotitan could not have been larger than Argentinosaurus because its back vertebrae were significantly shorter.
facts.quote: In 2019, Paul noted that the articulated length of the back vertebrae was larger in Argentinosaurus (4.47 m) than in Patagotitan (3.67 m), making it impossible for Patagotitan to have had a larger torso.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Matt Wedel criticized the methods used to compare Patagotitan and Argentinosaurus sizes, noting that the polygon-based models for Patagotitan included large areas of empty space.
facts.quote: Wedel also criticised the polygon-based method that Carballido and colleagues used to compare the sizes of Patagotitan and Argentinosaurus vertebrae, noting that the former was largely empty space.

facts.statement: The front and middle neck vertebrae of Patagotitan were extremely long, at least five times longer than they were wide at the rear.
facts.quote: The vertebrae in the front and middle portions of the neck of Patagotitan were very long, being at least five times as long as they were wide at the back

facts.statement: The rear neck vertebrae of Patagotitan featured deep pleurocoels, which are large openings on the sides that extend into the bone's interior.
facts.quote: By contrast, the rear neck vertebrae of Patagotitan had deep pleurocoels that opened from the sides into the interior of the bone

facts.statement: Patagotitan likely possessed 10 back vertebrae, similar to other titanosaurs with complete fossil records.
facts.quote: Like Futalognkosaurus and other titanosaurs that preserved a complete set of back vertebrae, Patagotitan probably had 10.

facts.statement: Patagotitan uniquely possessed nearly vertical prezygodiapophyseal laminae because its front joint processes sat higher than its side joint processes.
facts.quote: Uniquely, the prezygodiapophyseal laminae (PRDLs, which ran between articular processes, from the prezygapophyses at the front to the diapophyses at the sides) were nearly vertical because the prezygapophyses were situated higher up on the vertebrae than the diapophyses.

facts.statement: All neural spines in Patagotitan's back were tall and vertical, with the first few featuring expanded, arrow-shaped tips.
facts.quote: All of the neural spines in the back were tall and vertical in Patagotitan, and the first few had expanded, arrow-shaped ends.

facts.statement: The first two back vertebrae of Patagotitan uniquely show prespinal laminae that bulge outward near the bottom.
facts.quote: Uniquely, in the first two back vertebrae, the prespinal laminae that ran alongside the front of the neural spines bulged outwards near the bottom.

facts.statement: The third back vertebra of Patagotitan uniquely preserves a hyposphene at the rear but lacks a hypantrum at the front, suggesting the missing fourth vertebra had a hypantrum.
facts.quote: Also uniquely, the third back vertebra preserves a hyposphene at the rear end but not a hypantrum at the front; the missing fourth back vertebra presumably had a corresponding hypantrum.

facts.statement: Patagotitan is the first known sauropod to retain hyposphene-hypantrum articulations between only a single pair of vertebrae.
facts.quote: Hyposphene-hypantrum articulations to stiffen the vertebrae were primitively present among sauropods and lost multiple times, but Patagotitan is the first known sauropod where they were retained between only one pair of vertebrae.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the unique retention of hyposphene-hypantrum articulations in Patagotitan may have been a weight-bearing adaptation due to the position of the shoulder blade.
facts.quote: Because the shoulder blade was located at this position, this may have been a weight-bearing adaptation.

facts.statement: Patagotitan uniquely possessed a flat front articulating surface on its first tail vertebra, unlike other titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Uniquely in Patagotitan, the front articulating surface of the first tail vertebra was flat.

facts.statement: The neural spines of Patagotitan's front tail vertebrae were uniquely four to six times wider than they were long, contrasting with other titanosaurs where they were longer than wide.
facts.quote: Also uniquely, the neural spines of the front tail vertebrae were about four to six times as wide from side to side as they were long front to back, contrasting with the condition in Dreadnoughtus, Epachthosaurus, and Malawisaurus where they were longer front to back.

facts.statement: The neural spines of Patagotitan's front tail vertebrae were 1.5 times taller than the underlying vertebral bodies.
facts.quote: They were also tall, being 1.5 times taller than the underlying centra (vertebral bodies).

facts.statement: The tops of Patagotitan's front tail neural spines were uniquely concave, creating a bifurcated shape with tips curling forward.
facts.quote: Yet another unique characteristic was that the tops of the neural spines were concave, making them somewhat bifurcated with the tips curling forwards.

facts.statement: The transverse processes on the sides of Patagotitan's front tail vertebrae were high and thin, a trait shared with Futalognkosaurus and Mendozasaurus but distinct from Dreadnoughtus.
facts.quote: At the sides of the front tail vertebrae, the transverse processes (on which the diapophyses were located) were high and thin, like Futalognkosaurus and Mendozasaurus but unlike Dreadnoughtus and other titanosaurs.

facts.statement: The expanded transverse processes on Patagotitan's tail vertebrae provided larger muscle attachment areas, resulting in a more muscular tail.
facts.quote: These expanded transverse processes would have resulted in greater attachment areas for the caudofemoralis longus, ilio-ischiocaudalis, and spinalis muscles, and therefore a more muscular tail.

facts.statement: Patagotitan possessed a robust and expanded scapula blade that was only 4.15 times longer than it was wide at its narrowest point.
facts.quote: Patagotitan had a robust, expanded scapula, with the blade being only 4.15 times as long as it was wide at its narrowest point

facts.statement: The scapula of Patagotitan expanded at both ends, making the top and bottom ends roughly level with each other.
facts.quote: expansion was present at both ends such that the top end of the scapula was roughly at the same level as the bottom end

facts.statement: The acromion ridge on the scapula of Patagotitan was approximately 30% as long as the entire scapula.
facts.quote: the acromion ridge was about 30% as long as the scapula

facts.statement: A second ridge running diagonally upward to the top of the scapula blade was a unique characteristic found only in Patagotitan.
facts.quote: there was a second ridge that ran upwards diagonally to the top of the bone, which was unique to Patagotitan

facts.statement: The articulating surface between the coracoid and scapula in Patagotitan was 80% as long front-to-back as it was tall.
facts.quote: The articulating surface of the coracoid with the scapula was 80% as long front-to-back as it was tall

facts.statement: The humerus of Patagotitan was on average 28% as broad as it was long.
facts.quote: The humerus of Patagotitan was on average 28% as broad as it was long

facts.statement: The humerus of Patagotitan was approximately 70% as long as its femur.
facts.quote: it was about 70% as long as the femur

facts.statement: Patagotitan possessed a number of unique bulges on its humerus for muscle attachment.
facts.quote: A number of bulges for muscle attachment on the humerus were unique characteristics of Patagotitan

facts.statement: The ulna of Patagotitan was robust, measuring about 50% as broad at the top as it was long.
facts.quote: the ulna was robust, being about 50% as broad at the top as it was long

facts.statement: The bottom of the pubic boot in Patagotitan was not particularly expanded.
facts.quote: the bottom of the pubic "boot" was not particularly expanded

facts.statement: The femur of Patagotitan was robust, averaging 23% as broad as it was long.
facts.quote: the femur of Patagotitan was robust, being on average 23% as broad as it was long

facts.statement: A 2017 analysis placed Patagotitan as the sister group to Argentinosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2017, a phylogenetic analysis by Carballido and colleagues placed Patagotitan as the sister group to its closest relative, Argentinosaurus

facts.statement: Patagotitan and Argentinosaurus were grouped into Lognkosauria based on specific skull and tail vertebrae features.
facts.quote: These two were placed within the Lognkosauria, based on the SDLs, the tall transverse processes, and small laminae that connect the neural spine to the prezygapophyses

facts.statement: Lognkosauria, including Notocolossus and Bonitasaura, formed a sister group to Rinconsauria.
facts.quote: The group of lognkosaurs, Notocolossus, and Bonitasaura was recovered as the sister group of Rinconsauria

facts.statement: In 2022, researchers found Patagotitan had a 62% recuperation index, making it one of the most phylogenetically stable titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Due to its completeness, Carballido and colleagues in 2022 found that Patagotitan was among the most phylogenetically stable titanosaurs, with a high recuperation index of 62%

facts.statement: Researchers suggested dividing Eutitanosauria into Saltasauroidea and Colossosauria.
facts.quote: They suggested that Eutitanosauria be divided into Saltasauroidea and Colossosauria

facts.statement: Patagotitan is classified within the family Lognkosauria.
facts.quote: familia: Lognkosauria

facts.statement: The genus Patagotitan was named by Carballido and colleagues in 2017.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Carballido, Pol, Otero, Cerda, Salgado, Garrido, Ramezani, Cúneo, Krause, 2017

facts.statement: Patagotitan lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 101 million years ago in the Cenomanian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 101 millones de años durante el Cenomaniense

facts.statement: Patagotitan fossils were found in the Cerro Barcino Formation in Chubut Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Sus restos se hallaron en la Formación Cerro Barcino, en la provincia de Chubut, Argentina, en el centro de la Patagonia argentina

facts.statement: The discovery of Patagotitan fossils was announced in May 2014.
facts.quote: El hallazgo de sus restos óseos fue dado a conocer en mayo de 2014

facts.statement: Patagotitan was officially named in August 2017.
facts.quote: Recibió su nombre en agosto de 2017

facts.statement: Researchers claim Patagotitan would be the largest land animal of all time.
facts.quote: Los investigadores afirman que sería el animal terrestre más grande de todos los tiempos

facts.statement: Initial estimates suggested Patagotitan reached 37.2 meters in length and weighed 69 tonnes.
facts.quote: Según datos estimados, su tamaño sería de 37,2 metros de longitud y 69 toneladas de peso

facts.statement: Later mass estimates for Patagotitan range from 50 to 57 tonnes.
facts.quote: Aunque las estimaciones de masa posteriores indican una masa de 50 a 57 toneladas

facts.statement: Patagotitan lived in a forested region.
facts.quote: Patagotitan lived in what was then a forested region

facts.statement: A new genus of cypress, Austrocupressinoxylon, was named in 2019 from fossilized wood found near Patagotitan.
facts.quote: A new genus of cypress similar to the living Fitzroya and Pilgerodendron, Austrocupressinoxylon, was named from the fossilized wood in 2019

facts.statement: The fossilized cypress trees found near Patagotitan were estimated to be 15.3 meters tall.
facts.quote: These trees were estimated as having been 15.3 m tall

facts.statement: Sediments containing Patagotitan fossils indicate low-energy water flow on a floodplain.
facts.quote: The fine-grained sandstone and tuff-bearing siltstone sediments of the Cerro Castaño Member, from which the specimens of Patagotitan were uncovered, are indicative of low-energy water flow on a floodplain

facts.statement: Flooding was likely too weak to move Patagotitan bones, meaning the individuals were preserved where they died.
facts.quote: This flooding was probably too weak to transport the bones of Patagotitan, meaning that the individuals were preserved where they died

facts.statement: Other animals found in the same locality as Patagotitan include the theropods Tyrannotitan and Genyodectes, the crocodyliform Barcinosuchus, and the turtle Chubutemys.
facts.quote: Animals from other localities in the Cerro Castaño Member include the theropod dinosaurs Tyrannotitan and Genyodectes, the peirosaurid crocodyliform Barcinosuchus, and the cryptodire turtle Chubutemys

facts.statement: The evolutionary relationships of titanosaurs have historically been unstable and varied between analyses.
facts.quote: Historically, the interrelationships of titanosaurs have been highly unstable and varied between different analyses

facts.statement: A 2021 analysis suggested Ninjatitan might be closer to Patagotitan and Argentinosaurus than Puertasaurus.
facts.quote: In 2021, Pablo Gallina and colleagues recovered a similar arrangement, except with Ninjatitan possibly being closer to Patagotitan and Argentinosaurus than Puertasaurus

facts.statement: A 2023 analysis found Ninjatitan closer to Rinconsauria rather than Patagotitan.
facts.quote: In 2023, Agustín Pérez Moreno and colleagues performed an analysis based on that of Gallina and colleagues, and found a similar arrangement except with Ninjatitan closer to the Rinconsauria

facts.statement: Patagotitan lived during the Late Cretaceous, between 102 and 95 million years ago, in a forested region.
facts.quote: Vivió durante el Cretácico Superior, hace entre 102 y 95 millones de años, en lo que entonces era una región boscosa.

facts.statement: José Luis Carballido and Diego Pol described the discovery of Patagotitan in a video from the laboratories of the Egidio Feruglio Paleontological Museum.
facts.quote: En un video, José Luis Carballido y Diego Pol, contaron sobre el hallazgo, en los laboratorios del Museo Paleontológico Egidio Feruglio.

facts.statement: In 2014, news reports estimated Patagotitan's size at 40 meters long and 77 tons.
facts.quote: En 2014, los informes de noticias indicaron estimaciones de tamaño de 40 metros de largo con un peso de 77 toneladas.

facts.statement: Scientific writer Riley Black warned in 2014 that it was too early to make size estimates with the desired scientific certainty.
facts.quote: El escritor científico Riley Black había advertido en 2014 que aún era demasiado pronto para hacer estimaciones de tamaño con la certeza científica deseable.

facts.statement: Using a 3D skeletal model volumetric method, Patagotitan's weight was estimated between 44.2 and 77.6 tons.
facts.quote: y 44,2 a 77,6 toneladas cuando se utiliza el método volumétrico basado en modelos esqueléticos 3D.

facts.statement: Patagotitan's humerus was 1.67 meters long, smaller than those of Notocolossus (1.76 meters) and Paralititan (1.69 meters).
facts.quote: El húmero de Patagotitan tenía 1,67 metros de largo, más pequeño que el de otros gigantes como Notocolossus, 1,76 metros y Paralititan, 1.69 metros.

facts.statement: Researchers described Patagotitan as the largest known land animal based on bone sizes exceeding previous giants.
facts.quote: Los investigadores que describieron a Patagotitan declararon en los medios que Dado el tamaño de estos huesos, que superan a cualquiera de los animales gigantes conocidos anteriormente, el nuevo dinosaurio es el animal más grande conocido que caminó sobre la Tierra.

facts.statement: After Patagotitan's publication, Riley Black and paleontologist Matt Wedel warned against the media hype.
facts.quote: Tras la publicación de Patagotitan, Riley Black y el paleontólogo Matt Wedel advirtieron además contra el bombo mediático.

facts.statement: Matt Wedel noted that while Patagotitan was comparable to other giant titanosaurs, almost all comparable bone measurements are larger in Argentinosaurus.
facts.quote: Wedel señaló que, según las medidas disponibles, Patagotitan era comparable en tamaño a otros titanosaurianos gigantes conocidos, sin embargo, casi todas las medidas óseas que se pueden comparar son más grandes en Argentinosaurus.

facts.statement: The authors identified nine distinctive traits of Patagotitan.
facts.quote: Los autores indicaron nueve rasgos distintivos de Patagotitan.

facts.statement: On the first two rear vertebrae, the crest running down from the front lateral side of the neural arch has a bump on the bottom.
facts.quote: Con las dos primeras vértebras traseras, la cresta que corre hacia abajo desde el frente lateral de la columna neural tiene un bulto en la parte inferior.

facts.statement: Patagotitan has secondary hypospheno-hipantropophysis articulation processes, a complex type limited to the joint between the third and fourth back vertebrae.
facts.quote: Procesos de articulación secundarios del hiposfeno-hipantro. El tipo complejo se limita a la articulación entre la tercera y cuarta vértebra de la espalda.

facts.statement: The middle and posterior back vertebrae of Patagotitan have vertical neural spines.
facts.quote: Las vértebras de la espalda media y posterior tienen espinas neurales verticales.

facts.statement: The first tail vertebra of Patagotitan has a flat articulation facet on the front and a convex facet on the back of the main vertebral body.
facts.quote: En la primera vértebra de la cola, el centro o cuerpo vertebral principal tiene una faceta de articulación plana al frente y una faceta convexa en la parte posterior.

facts.statement: The front tail vertebrae of Patagotitan have neural spines where the transverse width is four to six times larger than their length measured from front to back.
facts.quote: Las vértebras de la cola delantera tienen espinas neurales cuyo ancho transversal es de cuatro a seis veces más grande que su longitud medida de adelante hacia atrás.

facts.statement: The front tail vertebrae of Patagotitan have neural spines that show some bifurcation.
facts.quote: Las vértebras de la cola delantera tienen espinas neurales que muestran alguna bifurcación.

facts.statement: Patagotitan's upper arm bone has a distinctive protuberance on the rear outer side.
facts.quote: El hueso de la parte superior del brazo tiene una protuberancia distintiva en el lado exterior trasero.

facts.statement: Patagotitan's femur has a straight edge on the outer side.
facts.quote: El fémur tiene un borde recto en el lado exterior.

facts.statement: Patagotitan was first described as a genus and species in 2017 by a team of researchers including José L. Carballido and Diego Pol.
facts.quote: Esta especie fue descrita originalmente junto con su género, en el año 2017 por los investigadores José L. Carballido, Diego Pol, Alejandro Otero, Ignacio A. Cerda, Leonardo Salgado, Alberto C. Garrido, Jahandar Ramezani, Néstor R. Cúneo y Javier M. Krause.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in the El Sombrero locality, about 260 kilometers southwest of Trelew in the Chubut River valley.
facts.quote: El lugar del hallazgo se sitúa en el paraje El Sombrero, departamento Mártires, al sur del río Chubut, zona cercana a la localidad de Las Plumas, dentro del valle de los Mártires, a unos 260 kilómetros hacia el sudoeste de Trelew.

facts.statement: A rural worker named Aurelio Hernández discovered the end of a giant femur sticking out of the ground in 2008 while riding on the 12,800-hectare La Flecha ranch.
facts.quote: En el año 2008, el peón rural Aurelio Hernández, fallecido en el año 2012, mientras hacía una recorrida a caballo por parte de las 12 800 hectáreas de la estancia «La Flecha», en plena meseta chubutense, observó que sobresalía del terreno el extremo de un gigantesco fémur.

facts.statement: Excavation of the bones began in January 2014, and the remains were deposited in the Museo Paleontológico Egidio Feruglio.
facts.quote: Finalmente en enero de 2014 pudieron comenzar a desenterrar los restos óseos, los que fueron depositados en el museo citado.

facts.statement: Scientists found fossilized remains of six other adult specimens alongside the main skeleton within deposits of the Chubut Group formation.
facts.quote: Los científicos descubrieron que junto al ejemplar se encontraban los vestigios petrificados de otros 6 especímenes (todos adultos), ubicados en un enorme campo de fósiles, que conservó restos con un inusual estado de preservación, inmersos en depósitos de la formación geológica «grupo Chubut».

facts.statement: The femurs found measured between 230 cm and 240 cm in length.
facts.quote: De los fémures encontrados, el menor midió 230 cm y el mayor 240 cm.

facts.statement: Seven field expeditions between January 2013 and February 2015 recovered over 200 fossils, including 57 teeth from theropods.
facts.quote: Entre enero de 2013 y febrero de 2015 se realizaron siete expediciones de campo paleontológicas al sitio fósil de La Flecha, recuperando más de 200 fósiles, tanto de saurópodos como de terópodos, representados por 57 dientes.

facts.statement: At least six partial skeletons containing about 130 bones were found, making Patagotitan one of the most complete titanosaurians known today.
facts.quote: Se descubrieron al menos seis esqueletos parciales, que constan de aproximadamente 130 huesos, lo que convierte a Patagotitan en uno de los titanosaurianos más completos que se conocen actualmente.

facts.statement: Fossilized tree trunks and plant impressions show that Patagotitan lived in a lush forest with trees up to 15 meters tall, contrasting with today's dry landscape.
facts.quote: Acompañaban a las muestras de estos animales, troncos fosilizados e improntas de la vegetación que convivió con los mismos, lo que permite reconstruir parte de su ecosistema, el que contrastaba netamente con el paisaje frío y seco de hoy, pues crecía un frondoso bosque con árboles de unos 15 metros de alto, de los cuales se alimentaban los titanosaurios.

facts.statement: The generic name Patagotitan combines a reference to Patagonia with a Greek Titan due to the animal's strength and large size.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico combina una referencia a la Patagonia con un Titán griego por la "fuerza y el gran tamaño" de este titanosauriano.

facts.statement: The species name mayorum honors the Mayo family, who owned the La Flecha ranch.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie honra a la familia Mayo, dueños del rancho La Flecha.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MPEF-PV 3400 was found in the Cerro Barcino Formation, dating to the late Albian stage.
facts.quote: El holotipo, MPEF-PV 3400, fue encontrado en una capa de la Formación Cerro Barcino, que data de finales del Albiense.

facts.statement: The specific layer containing the holotype is dated to approximately 101.62 million years ago, with a margin of error of 0.18 million years.
facts.quote: El estrato particular tiene una edad de 101,62 hace más o menos 0,18 millones de años.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton that lacks a skull.
facts.quote: El holotipo consiste en un esqueleto parcial que carece de cráneo.

facts.statement: The holotype includes three neck vertebrae, six posterior vertebrae, six anterior tail vertebrae, three chevrons, ribs, both breast bones, the right scapulocoracoid, both pubic bones, and both thigh bones.
facts.quote: Contiene tres vértebras del cuello, seis vértebras traseras, seis vértebras delanteras de la cola, tres cheurones, costillas, ambos huesos del pecho, el escapulocoracoideo derecho de la cintura escapular, ambos huesos púbicos y ambos huesos del muslo.

facts.statement: Fifty-seven teeth of the carnivorous dinosaur Tyrannotitan chubutensis were found nearby, suggesting they scavenged the herbivorous giants.
facts.quote: Junto a ellos se encontraron 57 dientes de Tyrannotitan chubutensis, un dinosaurio carnívoro que se postula que carroñaron los cuerpos de los gigantes herbívoros.

facts.statement: Three distinct but closely spaced burial horizons within 343 cm of sediment suggest three separate events where young adults died due to flooding.
facts.quote: Dentro del sedimento de 343 centímetros de espesor que contiene los fósiles, tres horizontes distintos pero estrechamente espaciados corresponden a tres eventos de entierro en los que los adultos jóvenes perecieron debido a las inundaciones.

facts.statement: The water covered the carcasses with sandstone and shale rather than transporting them further.
facts.quote: El agua no transportó más los cadáveres, sino que los cubrió con arenisca y lutita.

facts.statement: The animals were approximately the same size, differing by no more than 5% in length.
facts.quote: Los animales eran aproximadamente del mismo tamaño, y no diferían más del 5% en longitud.

facts.statement: In 2017, Patagotitan was classified within Titanosauria, specifically in Eutitanosauria and Lognkosauria, as a sister species to Argentinosaurus.
facts.quote: En 2017, Patagotitan se colocó, dentro de Titanosauria, en Eutitanosauria y más precisamente en Lognkosauria, como una especie hermana de Argentinosaurus.

facts.statement: Patagotitan lived during the Albian stage, between 113.2 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 100.5 million years ago)
